rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The well-known interpretation takes rāḍiya as a relational adjective: the life is one endowed with contentment or satisfaction.
rows.anchor: المشهور جعل ذلك من باب النسب أي ذات رضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also allows rāḍiya as a figurative passive meaning pleasing or pleased-with, or a figurative attribution whose true subject is the life’s possessor.
rows.anchor: أن تكون راضية بمعنى المفعول أى مرضية على التجوز في الكلمة نفسها وأن يكون الاسناد مجازيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A concealed metaphor with an imaginative metaphorical feature is another possible analysis, as discussed in works of rhetoric.
rows.anchor: وجوز ان يكون في الكلام استعارة مكنية وتخييلية على ماقرر في كتب المعاني

rows.speaker: بعض الاجلة
rows.claim: A distinguished scholar argues that relational adjectives mean ‘possessing such-and-such’ and therefore are not feminine, since they do not modify an expressed noun and are treated as nouns.
rows.anchor: ماكان للنسب يؤول بذي كذا فلا يؤنث لانه لم يجر على موصوف فالحق بالجوامد

rows.speaker: السيرافي
rows.claim: Al-Sīrāfī objects that the feminine h in ʿīsha rāḍiya challenges the claim that relational forms do not take feminine marking.
rows.anchor: نقل عن السيرافي انه قال يقدح فيما عللوا به سقوط الهاء في عيشة راضية

rows.speaker: السيرافي
rows.claim: One explanation makes the life pleased with its inhabitants, accompanying them and content with them.
rows.anchor: أن تكون بمعنى انها راضية أهلها فهي ملازمة لهم راضية بهم

rows.speaker: السيرافي
rows.claim: A second explanation treats the feminine h as an intensive suffix, as in ʿallāma and riwāya.
rows.anchor: والآخر أن تكون الهاء للمبالغة كعلامة ورواية

rows.speaker: السيرافي
rows.claim: The h may preserve the word’s form by preventing loss of yāʾ; similar weak adjectives and some forms otherwise not feminized show this usage.
rows.anchor: الهاء لزمت لئلا تسقط الياء فيخل بالبنية كناقة مشلية وكلبة مجرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi explains rāḍiya here as an active participle whose necessary implication is intended: whoever wants and accepts something necessarily stays with it; the attribution may also be figurative.
rows.anchor: راضية هنا فيه ليس من باب النسب بل هو اسم فاعل أريد به لازم معناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He accepts intensive h as an explanation, noting that this suffix is not confined to the pattern faʿʿāl, as riwāya also shows.
rows.anchor: ان الهاء للمبالغة ولا تختص بفعال ولذا مثل برواية أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also accepts adding h to a weak adjective to preserve its form; misakka is either an irregular form or reflects geminates’ resemblance to weak roots.
rows.anchor: يجوز الحاق الهاء في المعتل لحفظ البنية ومصكة اما شاذا ولتشبه المضاعف بالمعتل

rows.speaker: ابن زيد وغيره
rows.claim: ‘Its mother’ means his refuge or abode, according to Ibn Zayd and others.
rows.anchor: ( فأمه ) أي فماواه كما قال ابن زيد وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hāwiya means the Fire, as the following divine statement indicates.
rows.anchor: ( هاوية ) أريد بها النار كما يؤذن به قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers who act righteously make a trade that cannot perish, exchanging fleeting, inferior goods for lasting, precious ones and righteous deeds for passing pleasures.
rows.anchor: فانهم في تجارة لن تبور حيث باعوا الفاني الخسيس واشتروا الباقي النفيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ‘those who’ includes everyone meeting the description, not only ʿAlī and Salmān; Ibn ʿAbbās’s naming them makes them foremost examples, not an exclusive referent.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالموصول كل من اتصف بعنوان الصلة لا على كرم الله وجهه وسلمان الفارسي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is cited as mentioning ʿAlī and Salmān among those described as saved, and Abū Jahl as an example of the losing human; Alusi says neither example is exclusive.
rows.anchor: اقتصار ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما في الذكر عليهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mutual exhortation to truth completes the believers’ care for others: they enjoin what is established and undeniable, whose good effects endure in both abodes, including faith in God and following His books and messengers in belief and action.
rows.anchor: وصى بعضهم بعضا بالامر الثابت الذي لا سبيل إلى انكاره ولا زوال في الدارين لمحاسن آثاره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience means resisting sins desired by human nature, sustaining difficult obedience, and bearing the afflictions God ordinarily sends.
rows.anchor: عن المعاصي التي تشتاق اليها النفس بحكم الجبلة البشرية وعلى الطاعات التي يشق عليها أداؤها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience is already included in truth, but is repeated with its own preposition and verb to emphasize special concern for it.
rows.anchor: والصبر المذكور داخل في الحق وذكر بعده مع اعادة الجار والفعل المتعلق هو لابراز كمال العناية به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, truth is the rank of worship—doing what pleases God—while patience is the rank of servitude: accepting what God does.
rows.anchor: ويجوز ان يكون الاول عبارة رتبة العبادة اتي هي فعل مايرضى الله تعالى والثاني عبارة رتبة العبودية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience is more than restraining oneself from desired action or omission: it is receiving what comes from God graciously and being inwardly and outwardly content with it.
rows.anchor: ليس مجرد حبس النفس عما تتوق اليه من فعل أو ترك بل هو تلقي ما ورد منه عز وجل بالجميل

rows.speaker: سلام وهرون وابن موسى عن أبي عمرو
rows.claim: These transmitters read al-ʿaṣr with kasra on ṣād and al-ṣabr with kasra on bāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ سلام وهرون وابن موسى عن أبي عمرو والعصر بكسر الصاد والصبر بكسر الباء

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says this vowel transfer is permissible only when stopping.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية وهذا لايجوز الا في الوقف على نقل الحركة

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: A second transmission from Abū ʿAmr reads al-ṣabr with kasra on bāʾ and ishām; Ibn ʿAṭiyya likewise limits it to pause.
rows.anchor: وروى عن أبي عمرو بالصبر بكسر الباء اشماما وهذا كما قال لايكون أيضا الا في الوقف

rows.speaker: صاحب اللوامح
rows.claim: The author of al-Lawāmiʿ says ʿĪsā al-Baṣrī transferred the vowel of rāʾ to bāʾ in al-ṣabr, avoiding partial movement at pause and two consecutive vowelless letters; he calls it widespread Arabic, signaling inflection while preserving pause-sukūn.
rows.anchor: قرأ عيسى البصرة بالصبر بنقل حركة الراء إلى الباء لئلا يحتاج إلى أن يؤتى ببعض الحركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Baḥr cites the line ‘I am Jarīr, my kunya is Abū ʿAmr; I strike with the sword, and Saʿd at al-ʿaṣr’ as an example of this usage.
rows.anchor: اضرب بالسيف وسعد في العصر

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAbd b. Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir and others report that Companion ʿAlī recited an expanded form, adding ‘نوائب الدهر’ after al-ʿaṣr and extending the phrase with ‘إلى آخر الدهر’.
rows.anchor: عن علي كرم الله وجهه أنه كان يقرأوالعصر نوائب الدهر ان الانان لفي خسر

rows.speaker: ميمون بن مهران
rows.claim: ʿAbd b. Ḥumayd and Ibn Abī Dāwūd in al-Maṣāḥif report that Maymūn b. Mihrān recited the extended phrase ‘إلى آخر الدهر’; he identified it as Ibn Masʿūd’s reading.
rows.anchor: عن ميمون بن مهران أنه قرأ والعصر ان الانسان لفي خسر وانه لفيه إلى آخر الدهر

rows.speaker: بعض المعتزلة
rows.claim: Some Muʿtazilites infer that a major sinner remains eternally in Hell because the sura exempts from loss only believers who act righteously and exhort to truth and patience.
rows.anchor: استدل بعض المعتزلة بما في هذه السورة على ان مرتكب الكبيرة مخلد في النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi answers that the passage establishes only that those not excepted are in loss, not eternal punishment: loss may mean eternal residence for an unbeliever, entry into Hell for an unforgiven sinner, or lost high ranks if forgiven; he calls this a sound answer.
rows.anchor: وأجيب عنه بانه لا دلالة في ذلك على أكثر من كون غير المستثنى في خسر

rows.speaker: الماتريدى
rows.claim: Al-Māturīdī offers further responses in al-Taʾwīlāt, but Alusi calls them strained elaborations.
rows.anchor: وللشيخ الماتريدى رحمه الله تعالى في التفصى عن ذلك تكلفات مذكورة في التأويلات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sura plainly urges commanding right, forbidding wrong, and wishing for one’s brother what one wishes for oneself.
rows.anchor: وفي السورة من الندب إلى الامر بالمعروف والنهي عن النكر وان يحب المرء لاخيه مايحب لنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrat al-Humaza is Meccan and has nine verses, with no disagreement on either point.
rows.anchor: مكية وآيها تسع بلاخلاف في الامرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the previous sura says that humanity, except those specified, is in loss, this sura explains the conditions of some among the losers.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكر سبحانه فيما قبلها أن الانسان سوى من استثنى في خسر بين عز وجل فيها أحوال بعض الخاسرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘The one who gathered wealth’ may be an appositive to kull, a partitive appositive, or—according to al-Jarbardī—an adjective because kull is definite; Alusi questions that last analogy.
rows.anchor: ( الذي جمع مالا ) بدل من كل بدل وقيل بدل بعض من كل وقال الجار بردى يجوز أن يكون صفة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may instead be accusative or nominative as a construction of dispraise.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون منصوبا أو مرفوعا على الذم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite ‘wealth’ can magnify its quantity; those who say the sura was revealed about al-Akhnas report four thousand dinars, or ten thousand.
rows.anchor: وتنكير ملا للتفخيم والتكثير وقد كان عند القائلين انها نزلت في لاخنس أربعة لآلاف دينار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the indefinite can belittle the wealth as insignificant and contemptible before God.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون للتحقير والتقليل باعتبار أنه عند الله تعالى أقل وأحقر شىء

rows.speaker: الحسن وأبو جعفر وابن عامر والاخوان
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Abū Jaʿfar, Ibn ʿĀmir, and the two Ḥamzas read جمع with a doubled mīm, conveying repeated accumulation and fitting ‘he counted it repeatedly.’
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وأبو جعفر وابن عامر والاخوان جمع بشد الميم للتكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mainstream وعدده means that he counted the wealth repeatedly, out of love and intense attachment to it.
rows.anchor: أي عده مرة بعد أخرى حباله وشغفا به

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says he made the wealth into different classes and kinds, such as real estate and coins; this is cited in al-Taʾwīlāt.
rows.anchor: وقيل جعله أصنافا وأنواعا كعقار ونقوده حكاه في التاويلات

rows.speaker: غير واحد
rows.claim: Several commentators say he made the wealth a reserve stored for the calamities of time.
rows.anchor: وقال غير واحد أى جعله عة ومدخرا لنوائب الدهر ومصائبه

rows.speaker: الحسن والكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and al-Kalbī read وعدده with a light mīm, which can be a past-tense verb meaning ‘he counted it,’ with de-gemination contrary to regular analogy, as in the cited line.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن والكلبي وعدده بالتخفيف فقيل معناه وعده فهو فعل ماضي فك ادغامه على خلاف القيلس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited poetic line supplies a comparison for the lightened verb’s unusual de-gemination.
rows.anchor: كما في قوله مهلا اعاذل هل جربت من خلقي

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The lightened form may instead be the noun ‘number,’ coordinated with wealth: he gathered wealth, tallied its amount, and recorded it; counting already entails enumeration, so no strained ellipsis is needed.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو اسم بمعنى العدد المعروف معطوف على ماله أي جمع ماله وضبط عدده وأحصاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says both explanations of the lightened reading support the first interpretation of the mainstream reading.
rows.anchor: وعلى الوجهين ايد بالقراءة المذكورة المعنى الاول لقراءة الجمهور

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further view takes ʿadad as followers and supporters; coordinated with wealth, it means he gathered his assets and the people who defend him.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو اسم بمعنى الاتباع والانصار يقال فلان ذو عدد وعدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence is either circumstantial or a fresh sentence; akhladahu and khalladahu both mean that wealth left him everlasting, either without end or for an extremely long time.
rows.anchor: جملة حالية أو استئنافية وأخلده وخلده بمعنى أى تركه خالدا أى ماكثا لايتناهى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is a representational metaphor: wealth lengthens his hopes, so he builds, plants, and digs as though he thought it would keep him alive.
rows.anchor: والكلام من باب الاستعارة التمثيلية والمراد ان المال طول أمله ومناه الاماني البعيدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naming wealth explicitly where a pronoun could stand increases emphasis, and the past tense intensifies the intended meaning.
rows.anchor: والاظهار في مقام الاضمار لزيادة التقرير والتعبير بالماضي للمبالغة في المعنى المراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He may literally think wealth made him immortal because delusion and preoccupation with accumulation distract him from the terrors ahead, or because he believes life and safety depend on outward causes and wealth governs them.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يراد انه حاسب ذلك حقيقة لفرط غروره واشتغاله بالجمع والتكاثر عما امامه من قوارع الآخرة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reading says he counts wealth among the things that grant immortality, hinting that the truly worthy pursuit is the afterlife; Alusi calls this very far-fetched.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد انه يحسب المال من المخلدات ولانظر فيه إلى ان الخلود دنيوي أو اخروى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says the afterlife allusion is too far-fetched, and notes that a distinguished scholar did not treat it as an independent interpretation.
rows.anchor: والغرض منه التعريض بان ثم مخلدا ينبغي للعاقل أن يكب عليه وهو السعى للآخرة وهو بعيد جدا

rows.speaker: عصام الدين
rows.claim: ʿIṣām al-Dīn proposes that the subject of ‘made immortal’ is the hoarder and its object is wealth: he thinks he can preserve it forever, unaware that mishap or death will take it; Alusi rejects the proposal.
rows.anchor: وزعم عصام الدين أنه يحتمل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A saying warns that a miser’s wealth should expect a mishap or an heir, illustrating that he cannot keep it forever.
rows.anchor: كما قيل بشر مال البخيل بحادث أو وارث
